narrative_markdown:
## Today's Forecast

A high of 31°C / 88°F and an overnight low of 20°C / 67°F are expected today. Expect partly cloudy skies early, becoming mostly clear by midday and mostly cloudy into the evening. Thunder possible, peaking this evening. Winds will be north-northeasterly overnight, turning southwest by midday, with peak gusts up to 42 km/h (22 kt). The UV index will peak at 9.4, while air quality shows an AQI 79 (model estimate). As of 06:01, reports through 03:00: no rain; no thunder; high so far 22°C / 72°F; low so far 21°C / 70°F; peak sustained 7 km/h; sky partly cloudy.

## Extended Outlook

NEXT THREE DAYS: temperatures and winds much the same through Saturday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Thursday will be partly cloudy with three of four models wet and thunder likely. Friday stays partly cloudy with four of four models wet and thunder likely. Saturday brings mostly cloudy skies, four of four models wet, thunder likely, and a 100% rain chance. Highs spread across 27–33 °C through Saturday. Sunday will be mostly cloudy with three of four models wet and thunder likely. Monday features partly cloudy skies and four of four models wet. Tuesday remains mostly cloudy with three of three models wet and thunder possible. Wednesday finishes mostly cloudy with two of two models wet, thunder possible, and a 100% rain call.

## Severe Weather / Hazard Potential

Peak CAPE values indicate thunderstorm potential this evening, peaking at 18:00. Best Match reaches 2350 J/kg, ECMWF 2540 J/kg, ICON 3090 J/kg, and UKMO 4700 J/kg, all exceeding the thunderstorm threshold, while GFS remains lower at 670 J/kg. Any thunderstorm brings the hazard of sudden gusts well above the forecast wind. No severe weather warnings are currently active from the local meteorological service.

## Winam Gulf — Conditions for Boaters

On Winam Gulf, expect winds northeasterly overnight at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 8 km/h (4 kt), then south-southwesterly by midday at 7 km/h (4 kt) gusting 19 km/h (10 kt), then into the evening at 9 km/h (5 kt) gusting 21 km/h (11 kt); peak gust 31 km/h (17 kt). Where thunderstorms are possible, sudden gusts well above the forecast wind remain a hazard over the water.

## Detailed Discussion

### Synoptic Overview

Across roughly 2,600 km, pressure is lowest toward the north (1008 hPa) and highest toward the southeast (1014 hPa) — a 6 hPa spread, a moderate large-scale gradient. Pressure overhead is near-steady. Sampling is a nine-point ring at 12-degree spacing, so this locates a direction, not a centre or a front. Across 5 points, today's mean sea-level pressure sits between 1012.9 and 1015.2 hPa; near-steady over three days (-0.5 hPa). Overall pressure trend is -0.5 hPa with lower pressure toward the north.

### Forecaster Confidence Notes

At Day+0, no model is meaningfully better than the others yet across 51 checks. UKMO holds the best rain record at Day+0 with 80% accuracy, while ICON leads at Day+3 (73%) and ECMWF leads at Day+7 (73%), where GFS is the weakest rain caller. Today's call of 31°C / 88°F sits near GFS (31.8°C) and Best Match (31°C), whereas ECMWF (28.6°C) and ICON (29.8°C) run cooler due to known cold biases. GFS and ECMWF systematically under-forecast peak winds compared to the call's 42 km/h peak gust. The Kenya Meteorological Department (KMD) predicts a high of 30°C and low of 21°C with light showers and thunderstorms, broadly agreeing with the call. Verification coverage is settled at Day+0 and Day+7, with sufficient data at Day+3 to compare performance.

extended_outlook:
Temperatures and winds much the same through Saturday, with showers and thunderstorms likely each day. Skies partly cloudy Thursday and Friday, then mostly cloudy Saturday. Saturday's call: rain, 100%, with all four models wet; highs 27 to 32 °C. At this lead ICON has the best record, right 73% of the time over 67 checks.

Further out, temperatures and winds much the same through Wednesday, with showers and thunderstorms likely Sunday and Monday, and showers and thunderstorms possible Tuesday and Wednesday. Sunday: three of four models wet, highs 27 to 30 °C. Monday: all four models wet, highs around 30 °C. Tuesday: all three models that reach it wet, the week's wettest day at 11 mm on average, highs around 29 °C, thunder possible rather than likely.

Only GFS, ECMWF and ICON reach past Monday. ICON is the wetter solution from Sunday to Monday; GFS, ECMWF and UKMO keep it drier. Wednesday's call: rain, 100%, with both models wet; highs 28 to 31 °C. At this lead ECMWF has the best record, right 73% of the time over 63 checks.
